Calendar day-of-week name (proper noun) per ISO 8601:2019 § 3.1.1.2 and GPO Style Manual 2016 §9.20 (Months and days)
Citation abbreviation per GPO Style Manual 2016 Ch. 9 §9.4 / §9.6
Latin legal-text abbreviation preserved in U.S. legal English per Black's Law Dictionary 11th ed. (2019) and Bluebook 21st ed. §6.1
Latin biological-taxonomy class name (zoological) per International Code of Zoological Nomenclature 4th ed. (1999) and GPO Style Manual 2016 §11.20
Single- or two-letter abbreviation appearing in USC heading text per GPO Style Manual 2016 §9.4
Productive English prefix used as a standalone token (pre-, multi-, cyber-) per Huddleston & Pullum 2002 Ch. 19 §1.2
U.S. Federal-government agency acronym per Federal Register Document Drafting Handbook 2017 Ch. 4 §4.1 + U.S. Government Manual (annual)
U.S. territory (Puerto Rico, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, U.S. Virgin Islands, American Samoa) + Freely Associated States per ISO 3166-2:US + Compact of Free Association
Geographic name (country, region, city) per U.S. Government Manual (annual) heading conventions
Demonym or indigenous-people designation per GPO Style Manual 2016 §5.20
Statutorily-named corporation or named entity per U.S. Government Manual (annual)
English N+N compound per Huddleston & Pullum 2002 Ch. 19 §1.4 + Bauer 1983 §6.2
English prefixed compound (anti-/inter-/intra-/multi-/non-/post-/pre-/sub-/under-/in-/de-/para-/...) per Huddleston & Pullum 2002 Ch. 19 §1.2 + Bauer 1983 §6.1

English neo-classical compound built on a combining form (bio-/geo-/hydro-/micro-/tele-/neuro-/cyber-/co-/cranio-) per Bauer 1983 §6 (neo-classical compounds) + Huddleston & Pullum 2002 Ch. 19 §3 (combining forms)
U.S. legal term-of-art per Black's Law Dictionary 11th ed. (2019)
Tokenizer artefact from hyphenation / capitalization at word boundaries per GPO Style Manual 2016 Ch. 15
